note: A position in a plan's walk (SPEC 3.4). A plan owns its graph and its walk runs from node to node, so a plan ends at its own node and nothing else holds a handle part-way along one of its arcs. The same walk in a network's highlight is valid, which is why this rule is separate from every walk rule and needs its own case. A plan is its own highlight, so the plan is dropped where a highlight would be. The third plan runs node to node and carries a `pin`: a pin is a handle on a highlight drawn over a network, and a plan has none, so the same rule drops it and names the `pin` key. The first plan is the same plan ending at its node, and survives.

diagnostics.message_advisory: a plan's walk runs node to node, and this `to` is a position — the plan is dropped
a plan's walk carries no pin — the plan is dropped
